transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Morales (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM), Avery Brooks (Onboarding Engineer); Maya Singh (Helios Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (VP Eng), Leah Park (Cloud Architect), Samir Patel (Security)

Auto-generated summary: Quick kickoff to align on onboarding scope, decide on hosted vs private deployment for initial pilot, and schedule benchmarks and security review.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Morales, AE on the account. Happy to kick off, quick intros?
00:12 Maya (Helios): Hi, Maya here. Head of ML at Helios. We're excited to get started.
00:17 Carlos (Customer): Carlos Ruiz, VP Eng, I'll be overseeing the infra side.
00:23 Leah (Customer): Leah Park, Cloud Architect. I'll take the lead on network and VPC setup.
00:28 Samir (Customer): Samir Patel, security. I'll focus on compliance, SOC2 stuff.
00:33 Jordan: Great, and from Redwood we've got Ethan Liu, our solutions engineer, Priya our CSM, and Avery on onboarding. Ethan, do you want to run the agenda?
00:41 Ethan (Redwood SE): Yeah sure, thanks. Agenda — quick goals and success metrics, architecture options (hosted API vs private VPC vs on-prem), security checklist (SSO, KMS, audit logs), plan for initial performance benchmark, timeline and owners. We'll leave time for Q&A at the end.
00:55 Jordan: Goal for today is to confirm success criteria and pick the integration path for the pilot. Maya, what's top of mind?
01:04 Maya: We want the inference to hit p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens to be predictable — we have a internal threshold. Also data handling: logs can't contain PHI and must be retained per our policy.
01:18 Ethan: Understood. Two clarifying Qs — is the 250ms p95 for single-token response latency or for typical chat-like 256 token sequences?
01:27 Maya: For our microservice calls, typical prompt length will be ~50 tokens user + 50 tokens response. So end-to-end p95 under 250ms is what we'll target.
01:36 Carlos: On the infra side, we prefer a VPC-backed private deployment for initial pilot because of regulatory concerns, but we want a path to move to Redwood hosted later.
01:46 Leah: Yes, we can do private. We'll need details on peering, allowed egress IPs, and whether Redwood needs inbound access. Also curious about KMS integration.
01:56 Samir: For security, SOC2 plus SSO via SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS key support are must-haves. Also we have a formal security questionnaire coming from procurement.
02:06 Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll get you our SOC2 report and the security pack after the call. Jordan will also send the SSO guide. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in private deployments; Ethan can go into detail.
02:18 Ethan: Quick note on deployment options — hosted API is fastest to get started, no VPC work, but for data residency and KMS controls private is easier. In private mode we run a private control plane or customer-managed control plane depending on the package; for the pilot we'll propose Redwood Private with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. That gives you audit logs, SSO and isolation.
02:44 Maya: Sounds right. Timeline-wise, we'd like a live pilot in ~3 weeks if possible. Is that feasible?
02:50 Avery (Onboarding): 3 weeks is tight but doable if we get SSO details and VPC network info this week. Benchmarking will also need a small test dataset and access window.
03:02 Ethan: For the performance benchmark we'll run a handful of runs: 50-token prompts, 64 and 128 batch sizes, and an emulated traffic ramp. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We usually need a 2-4 hour test window with consistent network.
03:20 Carlos: We'll carve out a time window. Who will run the benchmark?
03:24 Ethan: Redwood will run it on the dedicated pilot nodes but we will need an API key for the pilot environment and a test harness. We'll share the harness link and instructions.
03:33 Leah: On network, we use strict outbound egress and NATs per account, so we need explicit IPs to whitelist. Also do you use TLS mutual auth or standard TLS?
03:44 Ethan: Standard TLS for the API plus mTLS can be added for private deployments; we can document both. For whitelisting we'll provide a small set of egress IPs that the data plane uses.
03:55 Samir: About logs — can you confirm audit logs include token-level metadata but we can configure redaction to avoid PHI?
04:02 Priya: Yes, logs can be configured; we have an option to redact or not store full prompt content. We'll include that in the security pack.
04:10 Maya: Great. Any cost model we should be aware of for private?
04:14 Jordan: Private has a platform fee plus usage, and we can set reserved capacity for predictable throughput. For the pilot we'll do a short-term reserved instance or burst pool depending on the load — Ethan will suggest a config after the benchmark.
04:26 Ethan: Early recommendation: start with a small dedicated pool for consistent latency, enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and use 8-bit quantized models if quality is acceptable to reduce cost.
04:39 Maya: We sometimes see subtle quality regressions with heavy quantization; we need to include a quality gate in the benchmark.
04:46 Ethan: Absolutely. We'll include a quality eval step with sample prompts to compare outputs between FP16 and q4/q8 variants.
04:54 Carlos: Procurement will want pricing and a clear SLO. Can you share your SLA for Dedicated/private pilot?
05:00 Jordan: We'll share the SLA doc. For pilots we typically offer a target uptime and latency SLOs in the contract. Procurement packet will be in the security pack.
05:10 (silence / typing)
05:20 Maya: Quick Q — integration pattern: do we call Redwood API directly from our services in the VPC, or do we route through a proxy?
05:27 Ethan: You can call directly over the peered VPC endpoint; many teams put a sidecar proxy for retries/rate limits. We'll provide recommended patterns in the architecture doc.
05:39 Leah: On that doc — can you share a sample terraform for peering and firewall rules?
05:44 Avery: Yes, we'll share Terraform snippets and a sample CloudFormation/ARM equivalent.
05:50 Samir: On encryption, we need confirmation on data at rest and in transit, and whether KMS keys are customer-controlled.
05:57 Ethan: In private deploys KMS can be customer-managed; data-at-rest encryption uses those keys. In transit is TLS. We'll note exact cipher and versions in the security pack.
06:08 Maya: Excellent. What's the pilot success criteria again?
06:12 Jordan: Recap — 1) p95 latency under 250ms for typical 100-token roundtrips, 2) quality parity within defined thresholds comparing FP16 to quantized model, 3) secure integration with SSO and KMS plus SOC2 artifacts completed, 4) pilot run and benchmark executed with owners signed off.
06:30 Carlos: That works. Timeline and milestones?
06:34 Priya: Week 0 (this week) — finalize network and SSO details. Week 1 — they provide VPC info and we spin up pilot environment. Week 2 — benchmark run and quality eval. Week 3 — review results and decide rollout.
06:53 Maya: We'll aim to provide network and SSO details by Friday.
06:57 Jordan: Great. Any blockers?
07:00 Samir: We need to confirm log-retention policy and ability to redact. Also our legal team will send the questionnaire; Leah will sync with them.
07:08 Jordan: We'll respond to the questionnaire and provide templates.
07:12 (short cross-talk)
07:20 Ethan: A quick technical note — if you want sub-250ms p95 at 100 token workloads, you may need a combination of dedicated GPUs with a low-latency model variant and caching. We'll test with both a standard 13B model and a distilled low-latency variant.
07:36 Maya: Fine. For the pilot we'll start with the 13B verified model and test the distilled.
07:42 Carlos: On cost, can we cap spend? We want a weekly cap during pilot to avoid surprises.
07:48 Jordan: Yes, we can set quotas and budget alerts. We'll include suggested quotas in the onboarding checklist.
07:55 Maya: Who should we loop in for procurement?
07:58 Carlos: I'll handle procurement; Samir will coordinate security.
08:02 Jordan: Awesome. Any final Qs?
08:05 Leah: One more — do you support bringing your own model artifacts for inference or must we use the Redwood catalog?
08:12 Ethan: We support customer model uploads in private deployments as long as the model format is compatible and licenses are in order. For hosted open-models we have curated variants. We'll document the upload process.
08:23 Maya: Okay that's helpful.
08:26 Jordan: Alright, quick recap of action items and next steps — Jordan to send SSO/SAML guide and the onboarding checklist, Ethan to schedule the benchmark and share the test harness, Leah to send VPC info, Samir to share security questionnaire and log requirements. We'll plan the benchmark run for July 28 as a tentative date.
08:47 Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:50 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and links.

Post-call notes:
- Links shared: onboarding checklist (link to drive), security pack placeholder (will attach after call), benchmark harness repo (link), Terraform samples placeholder.
- Action items reiterated in metadata above.

End of transcript.
